content: 1. Both sodium bicarbonate and pau d'arco enhance anticoagulation effects. Exercise caution and monitor closely when these agents are used together. 2. Pegaspargase amplifies the effects of aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate through pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination increases the risk of bleeding events. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of penbutolol due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use (>1 week) may exacerbate this interaction. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Penbutolol and aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate together increase serum potassium levels. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 5. Penicillin G aqueous and aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance or through plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of perindopril via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination may lead to renal function deterioration, especially in elderly or volume-depleted individuals. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 7. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate decrease the absorption and efficacy of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 2 hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 8. Phenindione and aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate both enhance anticoagulation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 9. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of phenoxybenzamine and phentolamine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs decrease prostaglandin synthesis, which may contribute to this interaction. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with phytoestrogens, increase anticoagulation. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of pindolol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use (>1 week) may exacerbate this interaction. Additionally, both agents increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate increase serum potassium, while pirbuterol decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with piroxicam, enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with potassium acid phosphate, potassium chloride, and potassium citrate, all increase serum potassium levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 15. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate increase pralatrexate levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with prasugrel, increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination is commonly used in cardiovascular disease management but requires close monitoring. 17. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of prazosin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs decrease prostaglandin synthesis, which may contribute to this interaction. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with prednisolone and prednisone, increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination increases the risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of probenecid through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of propranolol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use (>1 week) may exacerbate this interaction. Additionally, both agents increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with protamine, enhance anticoagulation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 22. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of quinapril through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination may lead to renal function deterioration, especially in elderly or volume-depleted individuals. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of ramipril through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination may lead to renal function deterioration, especially in elderly or volume-depleted individuals. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with reishi, enhance anticoagulation. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with reteplase, increase each other's toxicity through anticoagulation. This combination is commonly used in cardiovascular disease management but requires close monitoring. 26. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to oral forms. Separate administration of rilpivirine and antacids by at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after. For combination products like dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or 6 hours after. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of riociguat by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 1 hour. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with rivaroxaban, increase each other's toxicity through anticoagulation. Aspirin is known to increase bleeding risk, which may be exacerbated when used with rivaroxaban. Monitor for signs and symptoms of blood loss. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Sacubitril/valsartan and aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate both increase serum potassium levels. Additionally, aspirin reduces the effects of sacubitril/valsartan through pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs decrease the synthesis of vasodilating renal prostaglandins, affecting fluid homeostasis and potentially diminishing antihypertensive effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 30. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with salicylates (non-ASA), enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate increase serum potassium, while salmeterol decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with salsalate, enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the absorption and efficacy of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms. Separate dosing of tetracyclines from multivalent cation-containing products. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 34. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with sertraline, increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination increases the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding. SSRIs inhibit serotonin uptake by platelets. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with Siberian ginseng, enhance anticoagulation. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of silodosin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs decrease prostaglandin synthesis, which may contribute to this interaction. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid, may cause fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate. Co-administration with medications causing fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increases the toxicity of aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate. Co-administration with medications causing fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases (practically insoluble at pH >5). Separate administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir from antacids by at least 4 hours. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 41. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of sotalol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use (>1 week) may exacerbate this interaction. Additionally, both agents increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to oral forms. Administer sparsentan 2 hours before or after antacids. Antacids may decrease sparsentan exposure, reducing its efficacy. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 43. Spironolactone and aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate both increase serum potassium levels. Aspirin reduces the effects of spironolactone through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Spironolactone doses may need to be titrated to higher maintenance levels, and patients should be observed closely to ensure the desired effect is achieved. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with succinylcholine, increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with sulfamethoxazole, may increase each other's effects through plasma protein binding competition. Due to the high protein-binding capacity of both drugs, one may displace the other when co-administered, leading to an enhanced effect of the displaced drug. The risk is low with low-dose aspirin. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with sulfasalazine, enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with sulindac, enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of telmisartan through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination may lead to renal function deterioration, especially in elderly or volume-depleted individuals. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 49. Temocillin and aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance or through plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with tenecteplase, increase each other's toxicity through anticoagulation. This combination is commonly used in cardiovascular disease management but requires close monitoring. 51. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of terazosin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs decrease prostaglandin synthesis, which may contribute to this interaction. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate increase serum potassium, while terbutaline decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with ticagrelor, may interact. Maintenance doses of aspirin above 100 mg decrease the effectiveness of ticagrelor. After the initial loading dose of aspirin (usually 325 mg), use ticagrelor with a maintenance dose of aspirin of 75–100 mg. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the effects of timolol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use (>1 week) may exacerbate this interaction. Additionally, both agents increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with tirofiban, increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination is commonly used in cardiovascular disease management but requires close monitoring. 56. Tobramycin (inhaled) and aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid concurrent or sequential use to decrease the risk of ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 57. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with tolfenamic acid, enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with tolmetin, enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, along with tolvaptan, increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate increase serum potassium, while torsemide decreases it. The net effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor closely.
